xcode.device-support.name: Device debug files
xcode.device-support.line: Files Xcode made for devices you used
xcode.device-support.what: Files Xcode copies from an iPhone, iPad or other Apple device the first time you connect it, to debug apps on it.
xcode.device-support.if-removed: You can still build and run apps; Xcode copies the files again when you next debug on that device.
xcode.device-support.comes-back: Yes, when you connect a device on that version again, which takes a few minutes.
xcode.previews.name: Xcode previews
xcode.previews.line: Files Xcode makes to show previews
xcode.previews.what: What Xcode builds to show your SwiftUI previews.
xcode.previews.if-removed: Nothing is lost; the folder stays and what is inside goes to the Trash.
xcode.previews.comes-back: Yes, the next time you open a preview, which then takes longer.
xcode.simulator-caches.name: Simulator caches
xcode.simulator-caches.what: Files the iOS simulators keep to start faster.
xcode.simulator-caches.if-removed: Nothing is lost. Your simulators and their apps stay.
xcode.simulator-caches.comes-back: Yes, the next time a simulator starts, which then takes longer.
xcode.archives.name: Xcode archives
xcode.archives.line: Builds you archived to share or upload
xcode.archives.what: The builds you archived in Xcode to publish an app, with what you need to read its crash reports.
xcode.archives.made-by: Xcode, when you choose Product, then Archive.
xcode.archives.if-removed: You can no longer read that version's crash reports or publish that build again.
xcode.archives.comes-back: No, so keep the archives of every version people still use.
xcode.enabled.label: Xcode's files
xcode.enabled.description: Finds device support files, previews, simulator caches and archives that Xcode keeps, while Xcode and the Simulator are closed. They go to the Trash.
xcode.reason.device-support: Debug files for {platform} {version} take {size}. Xcode copies them again if you connect a device on this version.
xcode.reason.device-support-recent: Debug files for {platform} {version} take {size}. This is one of the newest versions here, so a device you use may need them; Xcode copies them again when you connect it.
xcode.reason.previews: Xcode's previews take {size}. Xcode builds them again when you open a preview.
xcode.reason.simulator-caches: The simulators' caches take {size}. They are made again the next time a simulator starts.
xcode.reason.archive: Archived on {date}, {size}. It holds the debug symbols of that build: keep it if that version is still in use.
xcode.left-out.special: A running program may be using it, so it is kept.
xcode.left-out.not-yours: Some of it belongs to macOS or another user, or is locked, so only an administrator can remove it.
xcode.left-out.no-system: Fresher could not list your open apps, so it keeps this. Scan again.
xcode.left-out.app-open: Xcode or the Simulator is open and may be using this. Quit them and scan again.
